transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2025-07-22; Start: 16:30 PDT; Duration: 58 min; Recording: https://fireflies.mock/rec/ff-20250722-aurora-7f4a9b.mp3
Attendees: Evan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM); Alex Rivera (Aurora CTO), Priya Desai (Eng Mgr), Samir Patel (SRE), Lina Gomez (Security)

[00:00] Evan Park (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Evan, I'll run the demo and Maya will walk through the console parts. Jordan's on for any account questions.
[00:12] Alex Rivera (Aurora): Hi, Alex here. We'll jump in if we have questions. Short on time but we've got key folks — Priya, Samir, Lina.
[00:18] Priya Desai: Hey all. We're primarily interested in isolating teams with project keys and enforcing quotas per product.
[00:25] Maya Chen (SE): Great. Today we'll demo org and project keys, per-key quotas (tokens/day, rps, concurrency), and how burst windows work. We'll also show Optimize recommendations to reduce unit cost.
[00:36] Samir Patel (SRE): Quick context — Aurora runs multi-tenant inference: a mix of short chat queries and longer summarization jobs. Peak qps ~450, average 120, and we want to avoid noisy neighbors.
[00:50] Evan: Perfect. High-level: Redwood supports top-level org keys for billing and governance, and project keys for per-team isolation. Keys attach to policies: rate limits, token quotas, and routing (hosted vs dedicated).
[01:05] Lina Gomez (Security): We need audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO mapping of owners. Also SOC2 evidence.
[01:12] Evan: We'll include SOC2 and the network diagram after the call. We support KMS/HSM and audit logs with per-key activations.
[01:22] Maya: Ok jumping into live console — note: small audio glitch. Opening Console > Organization > API Keys.
[01:28] [screen share noise] Maya: Here you can see an org key and three project keys: ingest-service, chat-frontend, batch-worker. For each key the UI shows current RPS (1m avg), daily tokens used, concurrency, and quota windows.
[01:44] Maya: Creating a new project key — name: pilot-ingest, assign to project 'ingest', set default policy. Policy options: Token/day cap, RPS cap, concurrent requests cap, and burst allowance. Burst is defined as N extra tokens within a short sliding window and then a cooldown.
[02:03] Priya: Can burst be per-minute or per-second?
[02:06] Maya: Yes, you can pick burst granularity: 1s, 10s, 1m sliding windows. Under the hood it's token-bucket like behavior. We also offer leaky-bucket style for steady throughput.
[02:18] Evan: Important difference — a burst window allows sudden spikes while preserving long-term quotas. If you want hard limits, use the Token/day hard cap and concurrency cap together.
[02:30] Alex: How do we map keys to billing? We want per-team chargebacks.
[02:33] Evan: Each project key is tagged with billing metadata — cost center, team, and project. Console exports token usage CSV by tag; we can also push to your billing S3 or connect to your finance tool.
[02:45] Alex: Good. What about shared deployment — can one key route to Dedicated while another uses Hosted?
[02:49] Maya: Yes, routing policies let you pin a key to a deployment profile. You can route critical keys to Dedicated pool with reserved GPUs, and send non-critical to hosted. Automatic fallback routes exist if capacity is low.
[03:05] Samir: If Dedicated runs out, how's the graceful degradation?
[03:08] Maya: Policy-based fallback — you can set fallbacks to a lower-cost model or a hosted pool; requests get retried with backoff. There are SLA and latency differentiators.
[03:18] Evan: Now rate limiting specifics: RPS cap enforces per-second throughput; concurrency cap prevents huge parallelism at model level; token/day controls cost. For burst we allow a short window with higher RPS but it consumes from the same daily bucket.
[03:34] [05:00] Maya: Demo: set pilot-ingest token/day to 5M, RPS 200 average, concurrency 40, burst +100 tokens over 30s. Save. That policy will throttle at the RPS threshold but allow short spikes until the token/day budget is used.
[03:58] Priya: What happens when a key hits its daily cap? Responses? 429?
[04:02] Maya: 429 with structured JSON body indicating reason: quota_exceeded, and headers telling when quota resets. You can also configure soft-limits (warn then block) and webhooks for alerts.
[04:15] Alex: Can we do per-endpoint quotas? Example: summarization endpoint has heavy tokens — want stricter limits than chat.
[04:22] Maya: Yes, per-route policies are supported. You can attach route-specific token multipliers or separate quotas. Example: route /v1/summarize uses a multiplier x2 on token usage for quota accounting.
[04:34] Samir: How accurate are the token counts? We use variable-length encoders across models.
[04:38] Evan: Tokenization is model-aware in the platform. We expose both tokens and estimated cost. There are small rounding differences but within 1-2%.
[04:47] Priya: What about K/V cache or prefix cache affecting cost? We have a lot of repeated system prompts.
[04:52] Maya: Redwood has automatic prefix/KV caching. In Optimize we'll recommend cache-friendly prompt patterns; caching can cut token usage substantially. We'll show examples in the Optimize tab.
[05:02] [05:10] Maya: Switching to Optimize workspace — here's a workload analysis we ran on a synthetic trace. Optimize suggests: enable int8 quantization for batch-worker, set batch size to 8 for chat-frontend at p95 latency budget, and enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts. It estimates 18-28% cost savings.
[05:28] Alex: Those are good numbers. Any latency tradeoff with int8?
[05:31] Maya: Slight quality/latency tradeoff for some models, but on our curated list quantized variants meet MCRT thresholds; recommended with monitoring.
[05:40] Lina (Security): For KMS — do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:44] Evan: Yes, we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM providers. Keys can be rotated and we log key usage events.
[05:52] Lina: Audit logs retention?
[05:55] Jordan Li (CSM): We have configurable retention—30, 90, 365 days as add-ons. For enterprise we can do longer with archive options.
[06:05] Priya: A bit of nit: network egress and VPC peering — if we go private, can we run VPC-only control plane?
[06:12] Evan: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem deployments. For fully air-gapped we have a packaged private control plane option. We'll include the deployment checklist.
[06:21] Samir: About enforcement latency — is rate limit check in-line or async? We need sub-ms for edge gating.
[06:27] Maya: Rate checks are enforced at the gateway with in-memory counters for hot keys, and backed by a consistent store for global quotas. For sub-ms gating we recommend colocating the gateway in the same region.
[06:38] Alex: Any customers doing chargeback by team?
[06:41] Evan: Yes, plenty. We export per-key usage and labels; some customers push usage to their internal billing systems nightly.
[06:48] Priya: Ok, let's talk pilot shape — we want to run 1-week pilot for ingest and chat projects, validate throughput and billing. What do you need?
[06:56] Maya: We'll need sample traffic traces and three keys: ingest-test, chat-test, batch-test. We can provision a dedicated small pool for pilot or run on hosted with dedicated routing if you prefer.
[07:07] Alex: Likely start hosted then move to dedicated if predictable.
[07:10] Evan: Sounds good. We'll send a proposal with both options and the price delta.
[07:14] [07:20] Lina: Please include SOC2 cert and encryption at rest details in the packet.
[07:24] Evan: Will do.
[07:26] Jordan: I'll set up pilot kickoff invite once we get the traffic patterns.
[07:30] Priya: One last question — rate-limits for internal vs external customers? We want different tiers internally.
[07:35] Maya: You can create tag-based policy inheritance: internal-tag gets doubled quotas or no cost accounting depending on your policy.
[07:42] Alex: Great. 
[07:43] Evan: Recap of next steps: Evan send SOC2 + security brief + pricing, Maya share console walkthrough + policy templates, Aurora provide traffic traces and pilot projects, Jordan will calendar kickoff.
[07:56] Alex: Thanks everyone very useful.
[08:00] Evan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the packet and action items.

Transcript notes: Some ASR mis-heard model names (e.g., 'Redwood Optimize' sometimes shows as 'Redwood Opti-mize'); speaker labels may be slightly off in places; timestamps approximate.

End of transcript.
